### Summary

snapy's moist equations of state do not carry their own thermodynamics: they hold a kintera `ThermoY` module and
call it to convert between density, internal energy, pressure and temperature, and to evaluate heat capacities.
This section lists those calls and the state each one receives. Its content rests on source reading only.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Conversions of @sec-ch03 called by snapy's equation of state.

**Data.** Density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], mass fractions [-], internal energy [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$], $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa].

**Placement.** Every primitive/conserved conversion in snapy's moist equations of state.

**Activation.** The thermodynamics card of the snapy input; always on for a moist equation of state.

**Guarantee / limits.** Species order of `ThermoY` options: vapors, then clouds; dry species first in the state.

**Evidence.** No kintera test; see the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: this section maps call sites. The thermodynamic functions themselves are derived in @sec-ch03.

### Numerical method

snapy's moist equation of state creates its module with `ThermoYImpl::create` ([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:20`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L20)), and converts with `compute` and string keys such as `DY->V`, `VU->T`, `VT->P`, and
calls the free functions `eval_cv_R`, `eval_cp_R`, `eval_czh` and `eval_czh_ddC` for heat capacities and
compressibility terms ([`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:245-262`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L245-L262)). Before it reads species names and molar masses, the equation of state calls
`populate_thermo` ({{< code src/species.cpp populate_thermo >}}, [`snapy equation_of_state.cpp:128`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L128)), so that it uses the copy of the species
table held by its own options rather than kintera's process-wide table. Output diagnostics call
`relative_humidity` ({{< code src/thermo/relative_humidity.cpp relative_humidity >}}, [`snapy load_diag_output_data.cpp:113`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/output/load_diag_output_data.cpp#L113)).

The figure of the call graph is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.
